name: gemstone-ide
description: GemStone/S IDE for Visual Studio Code
author: James Foster

enumDescriptions: Editor-tab Spotter: a webview in an editor tab with labeled scope tabs, a source-preview pane, own match highlighting, and an always-on case indicator.
Bottom-panel view (default): the same webview docked in the panel strip (next to Terminal/Output). Stays out of the way; results open in the editor area above it.
gemstone.omniSearch.ui.markdownDescription: Which GemStone Search experience to open: the **bottom panel** view (default) or the editor-tab **Spotter**.

enumDescriptions: Subsequence match: the typed characters appear in order (the Quick-Open feel).
The typed text appears as a contiguous run.
The result starts with the typed text.
gemstone.omniSearch.matchMode.markdownDescription: How your typed query is matched against the names in each category: classes, method selectors, dictionaries, globals and class categories. **Source** and **Literals** match on the stone instead (whole method source / literal frames), so this setting does not affect them.

enumDescriptions: Class names.
Method selectors (queries the stone as you type).
SymbolDictionary names.
Global variable names.
Full method source (heavyweight; explicit scope only).
Methods referencing a literal you type, e.g. #at:put: (heavyweight; explicit scope only).
Class category names — not method categories (heavyweight; explicit scope only).

gemstone.omniSearch.categories.markdownDescription: Which search scopes GemStone Search includes. Narrow a single search on the fly with the scope tabs above the results; the Clear-filter button resets to searching everything. **Source** (full method-source search), **Literals** (methods referencing a compilable literal you type, e.g. `#at:put:`) and **Class Categories** (class-category names) are heavyweight, so they never run in the default search — pick their tab to use them.

gemstone.omniSearch.debounceMs.description: Delay after a keystroke before searching, in milliseconds (throttles per-keystroke stone queries).

gemstone.omniSearch.methodMinQueryLength.description: Minimum characters before the Methods category queries the stone (method search hits the stone per keystroke). Raise it if per-keystroke method search feels slow on a large stone; lower it (to 1) to search selectors from the first character.

gemstone.omniSearch.maxServerScan.markdownDescription:
How many matches the **Methods** search collects from the stone before it stops looking.

That search walks every selector of every class in your symbol list, so it gives up early to keep searching-as-you-type fast. This is a limit on the *results*, not just on the time: when a search stops here, no amount of **Load more** or **Load all** can reach the matches beyond it — the footer says `Methods scan capped at 200` when that happens.

Raise it to cast a wider net on broad terms (`add`, `at:`), at the cost of a slower search on every keystroke. Narrowing your search term is usually faster than raising this.

gemstone.omniSearch.referencesInPreview.markdownDescription: Show a row's references/senders (Alt+Enter or the ↗ button) as a sticky list in the right-hand preview pane, leaving the results list in place — click an entry to open its source. Turn this **off** to use the classic behavior, where references replace the whole results list (a pivot you back out of with ← / Esc).

gemstone.omniSearch.previewPane.markdownDescription: Show the source preview beside the results, filling in as you move down the list. The pane takes about **45%** of the width, which the bottom panel — wide but short — can least afford, so turning it off gives that room back to the result labels and also stops the per-row source fetches. This is the value the panel **starts** with; the ◧ button in the panel switches it for the current session without changing this setting.

gemstone.omniSearch.excludeFromAll.markdownDescription: Scopes to leave out of the **All** search while keeping their own tab, so you can still search them on purpose. Useful for **methods**, which queries the stone on every keystroke. This is different from `#gemstone.omniSearch.categories#`, which removes a scope altogether (no tab, no search). Source, Literals and Class Categories are always outside All and so cannot be listed here. This is the value the panel **starts** with; the **Scopes** button in the panel changes it for the current session without changing this setting.

enumDescriptions: Never number step points.
Number step points while a debug session is running (default) — they are what you want when reasoning about where execution is, and clutter the rest of the time.
Always number step points in GemStone method source.
gemstone.stepPoints.display.markdownDescription: When to number step points in GemStone method source, drawn as inlay hints. Each number is clickable and toggles a breakpoint at that step point. Whatever this is set to, hovering a step point always reports its number, and `#gemstone.breakpoints.toggleStepPoints#` flips the numbers on or off. Use the editor's own `#editor.inlayHints.enabled#` to restyle or suppress inlay hints everywhere.

gemstone.gciLibraries.description: Paths to GCI libraries, keyed by GemStone version (e.g. "3.7.4.3": "/path/to/libgcirpc-3.7.4.3-64.dylib")

gemstone.maxEnvironment.description: Maximum method dictionary environment to show when listing methods (0 = standard Smalltalk only, 2 = show environments 0–2). Applies wherever methods are listed — the GemStone Explorer, the System Browser, and hover, CodeLens, and Go to Definition.

gemstone.explorer.groupMethodsByCategory.description: Group methods in the GemStone Explorer's Methods pane under their categories. Turn off to list a class's methods flat, without the category level. Toggle quickly from the Methods pane title bar.

gemstone.sessionMode.description: Number of concurrent GemStone sessions allowed. 'single' (default) keeps one session at a time for a clearer mental model — the connected login shows an inline Logout action and the Sessions panel is hidden. 'multiple' (beta) re-enables concurrent sessions and the Sessions panel.

gemstone.exportPath.description: Root path for the local class mirror (read-only .gs files used by Find in Files / Go to Definition). Variables: {workspaceRoot}, {session}, {host}, {stone}, {user}, {index}, {dictName}. Defaults to {workspaceRoot}/.gemstone/{host}/{stone}/{user}/{index}-{dictName} — keyed by connection target so it is shared across that target's sessions and kept (and re-synced incrementally) across logout.

gemstone.classSync.readOnlyMirror.description: Write the local class-mirror .gs files as read-only, so they aren't edited directly (edit via the GemStone Explorer instead). Turn off to roughly halve the filesystem operations per class, which can noticeably speed up syncing on slow or network filesystems.

gemstone.rootPath.description: Root directory for GemStone installations and databases. Supports ~ for home directory.

jasper.mcp.registerWithClaudeDesktop.description: Automatically register the jasper MCP server with Claude Desktop. When enabled, Jasper writes a single user-scope `jasper` entry into Claude Desktop's global `claude_desktop_config.json` on activation (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/, Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\, Linux: ~/.config/Claude/). The entry stays put across VS Code restarts. Claude Code registration writes to `~/.claude.json` and is always on.

jasper.mcp.httpPort.description: Port on 127.0.0.1 where Jasper serves the MCP HTTPS/SSE surface. The URL to paste into connector UIs (e.g. Claude Desktop's 'Add custom connector') is https://127.0.0.1:<port>/sse. Jasper generates a self-signed TLS certificate on first run and stores it in the extension's global storage directory; trust it once via the 'GemStone: Install MCP TLS Certificate' command. First-come-first-served across VS Code windows — override this per-workspace in .vscode/settings.json to run multiple windows simultaneously.

sync_classes.description: Sync this connection's classes to the local .gemstone mirror (read-only .gs files for Find in Files / Go to Definition). Defaults to true; turn off for slow/remote connections.

gemstone.enhancedInspectorPerfTracking.description: Enable enhanced inspector perf tracking: count GCI round trips in the enhanced inspector. When enabled, shows a status bar counter and logs to the 'GemStone Enhanced Inspector Perf' output channel. Intended for performance tuning only.

enumDescriptions: After adding a dependency while connected, offer to load the project so the database has its code.
Load the project automatically after adding a dependency.
Never offer to load after adding a dependency.
gemstone.rowan.loadAfterAddingDependency.description: What to do after adding a dependency to the open Rowan project while a database is connected. Adding a dependency only writes files on disk; the database does not have the code until the project is loaded. Only applies while connected. The buttons on the prompt update this setting.

enumDescriptions: When a login fails because its database is not running, offer to start the database and then connect.
Start a stopped database and connect, without asking.
Never offer to start a database; report the login failure as-is.
gemstone.autoStartDatabase.description: What to do when a login fails because the database it connects to is not running. Only applies to local databases Jasper manages — a remote or hand-rolled stone is never started. Starting a database starts both its stone and its NetLDI. The buttons on the prompt update this setting.

enumDescriptions: Non-destructive: show the result as an inline annotation that is not part of the document, so the file is never modified. Hover the result for Copy and Expand actions.
Classic: insert the result into the document as editable text (a single Backspace removes it). This dirties the file.
gemstone.displayItMode.description: How 'Display It' (Ctrl+K D / Cmd+K D) shows its result.

enumDescriptions: When a stone lacks the recommended support, show one Install / Not Now / Always / Never prompt on connect.
Install the recommended support automatically on connect (uses the SystemUser default password; a notification explains if it must be entered).
Never offer or install the recommended support.
gemstone.serverSupport.autoInstall.markdownDescription:
What Jasper does when you connect to a stone missing the recommended server-side support — the **Enhanced Inspector** (GemStone 3.7.5+) and the **refactoring engine** (all releases), installed together: `ask` shows one Install / Not Now / Always / Never prompt, `always` installs silently, `never` does nothing. Installing needs a SystemUser login and commits the supporting classes to the database.

▶ [Install GemStone support now](command:gemstone.installServerSupport)

▶ [Uninstall GemStone support](command:gemstone.uninstallServerSupport) — removes both from the stone (does nothing if neither is installed; also needs a SystemUser login and commits the removal)

gemstoneSmalltalk.formatter.spacesInside.description: Add spaces inside parentheses: ( x ) instead of (x)
Add spaces inside brackets: [ x ] instead of [x]
Add spaces inside braces: { x } instead of {x}

gemstoneSmalltalk.formatter.spacesAround.description: Add spaces around the assignment operator: x := y instead of x:=y
Add spaces around binary selectors: a + b instead of a+b

gemstoneSmalltalk.formatter.spaceAfterCa.description: Add space after return caret: ^ x instead of ^x

gemstoneSmalltalk.formatter.blankLineAft.description: Insert a blank line between the method pattern and body

gemstoneSmalltalk.formatter.maxLineLengt.description: Maximum line length for wrapping (0 = no wrapping)

gemstoneSmalltalk.formatter.continuation.description: Additional indentation for continuation lines (multi-keyword messages)

gemstoneSmalltalk.formatter.multiKeyword.description: Split keyword messages to multiple lines when keyword count reaches this threshold

gemstoneSmalltalk.formatter.removeUnnece.description: Remove unnecessary parentheses based on Smalltalk message precedence (unary > binary > keyword, left-to-right)

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with GemStone
walkthroughs.description: Download GemStone, create a database, connect, and explore Smalltalk expressions in Jasper.

steps.title: Download GemStone and create a database
steps.description:
New here? Quick Setup downloads a GemStone version, creates a database, starts the stone, and adds a login — all in one step.
[Quick Setup](command:gemstone.quickSetup)

steps.title: Connect to a stone
steps.description:
Quick Setup already added a login — click it in Logins & Sessions to connect. To reach a stone you set up yourself, or a remote one, add a login first.
[Add a Login](command:gemstone.addLogin)

steps.title: Open a workspace
steps.description:
Open a scratch buffer to try out Smalltalk expressions.
[Open Workspace](command:gemstone.openWorkspace)

steps.title: Run your first expression
steps.description:
Select an expression and Display It to evaluate it inline.
[Display It](command:gemstone.displayIt)

steps.title: Inspect an object
steps.description:
Inspect It opens the result in the Inspector to drill into its fields.
[Inspect It](command:gemstone.inspectIt)

steps.title: Browse classes
steps.description:
Open the GemStone Explorer and click a class — its methods appear in the Methods pane below. Or jump straight to any class by name.
[Find Class…](command:gemstone.findClass)

steps.title: Search your code
steps.description:
One box searches across classes, methods, and method source — the fastest way to find something when you don't know where it lives.
[GemStone Search…](command:gemstone.search)

steps.title: Install recommended server support
steps.description:
Jasper can install two recommended server-side supports: the Enhanced Inspector (rich object views, GemStone 3.7.5+) and the refactoring engine (rename instance variable, and more). On connect it offers to install whatever a stone is missing; the `gemstone.serverSupport.autoInstall` setting (ask / always / never) controls that.
[Install GemStone Support…](command:gemstone.installServerSupport)

[Uninstall GemStone Support…](command:gemstone.uninstallServerSupport) removes both from the stone (does nothing if neither is installed).

scripts.compile: npm run compile:client && npm run compile:bin && npm run compile:server && npm run compile:mcp
scripts.//dev:fresh: Launch a fresh, isolated dev editor window: isolates gemstone.rootPath to an empty dir so it opens in a clean brand-new-user state (no downloaded servers or stones). Leaves HOME untouched, so the jasper MCP integration keeps working.
scripts.//dev:fresh:keep-installs: Like dev:fresh but reuses your real ~/Documents/GemStone so you can connect to servers/stones you've already downloaded.
scripts.//lint:gci-headers: Asserts vendor/gci-headers/versions.md matches the committed header files (hashes, folder links, and no unreferenced folders). Run after adding a row.
scripts.//lint: Results are cached under node_modules/.cache/eslint/, keyed on file content; run lint:cache:clear to force a full re-check.
scripts.//format: Results are cached under node_modules/.cache/prettier/, keyed on file content; run format:cache:clear to force a full re-check.
scripts.//hooks:install: Opt-in: installs local git pre-commit hooks (lefthook.yml) that lint staged files before each commit. Not run automatically by `npm install` — CI is the gate regardless of whether a dev installs these.
scripts.//test:gci: Runs only the on-demand 'gci' vitest project (client/vitest.config.ts); needs a live test stone (npm run test:server:start). `npm test` runs the 'default' project and excludes these.
scripts.test:gci: cd client && npx vitest run --project gci
scripts.//test:acceptance: End-user acceptance tests that drive a real VS Code window (Playwright + Electron). Slow and GUI-bound, so excluded from `npm test`. Run `npm run compile` first.
scripts.publish: npm run publish:vsce && npm run publish:ovsx
